inputs.root_cause: Per Event 234's next-action ranking, surveyed ORA's remaining 13 unresolved obligations (untouched this whole session). SAL-ORA-OBL-8EDD775BF1715438 (ORA-STREAM-001) has a narrow rule_text distinct from its capability sibling's much larger streaming-feature rule_text: 'The required stack.xml archive member is a UTF-8 encoded XML document conforming to the OpenRaster Layer Stack format.' Read codec/stack_xml.py::parse_stack directly and found it fed raw archive bytes straight to ElementTree.fromstring with no encoding check of any kind.
inputs.acceptance_evidence: 5 new tests prove: a stack.xml declaring a non-UTF-8 encoding is refused; genuinely non-UTF-8 bytes are refused even with no declaration present; explicit and case-insensitive UTF-8 declarations parse normally; undeclared genuine UTF-8 bytes (including non-ASCII content) parse normally.
inputs.regression_tier: full ora package suite (tests/python/ora) plus 6-format regression

execution_steps: 1. Surveyed ORA's 13 unresolved obligations (6 partial, 7 missing) and read each one's rule_text directly rather than trusting the shared proof_requirements template some obligations under the same capability share -- confirmed SAL-ORA-OBL-8EDD775BF1715438's actual rule_text is narrow (stack.xml UTF-8 + format conformance) and distinct from its capability sibling SAL-ORA-OBL-F8A3777A56AA6121's much larger streaming/lazy-access/resource-budget rule_text, even though both share the same generic proof_requirements text.
2. Read codec/stack_xml.py::parse_stack directly before writing any test and found no encoding handling at all -- payload bytes go straight to ElementTree.fromstring(payload).

3. Probed directly (before any fix): a stack.xml with an XML declaration naming encoding="ISO-8859-1" and correspondingly-encoded bytes parsed successfully via parse_stack, silently accepting a real spec violation. A second probe with genuinely non-UTF-8 bytes and NO declaration at all also parsed successfully, silently producing mojibake (a corrupted layer name) instead of a refusal. Both confirmed real, previously-unenforced gaps -- not merely untested behavior.

4. Added _require_utf8() to codec/stack_xml.py: first checks the XML declaration's encoding pseudo-attribute (extracted via a regex anchored to the start of the payload, since the XML spec requires it on the first line if present) and rejects any value that is not case-insensitively 'utf-8'; then independently attempts payload.decode('utf-8') and rejects a UnicodeDecodeError, catching the undeclared-mojibake case the declaration check alone would miss (a document with no declaration at all defaults to UTF-8 per the XML spec, so undeclared-but-non-UTF-8 bytes are a distinct violation).
5. Wired _require_utf8(payload) into parse_stack immediately after the existing reject_unsafe_xml() call, before the ElementTree parse.

6. Re-ran the two prior probes to confirm both are now refused with a clear error naming the actual declared encoding, and added three more probes (explicit UTF-8 declaration, case-insensitive 'utf-8' declaration, undeclared genuine UTF-8 with non-ASCII content) to confirm none of the valid cases regressed.

7. Wrote 5 formal tests in the existing test_obligation_stack_and_document.py (the file that already owns all other stack.xml parsing tests, including a pre-existing UTF-8-declared HEADER fixture), all passing on the first attempt.

8. Ran ruff (clean), the full ora suite (316 passed, was 311, +5), and the full 6-format regression (3381 passed, was 3376, +5; same 4 pre-existing unrelated safetensors interop failures, 2 skipped) confirming zero cross-format regression.

9. Ran skills-first governance: resolve -> add-python-api (COMPOSE_EXISTING_SKILLS), manifest create --write (sfx-02cb85f63355ab5b, confirmed as the actually-persisted manifest via ls -t .local/skills-first/manifests/), hand-written receipt YAML, closeout --close -> CLOSE_OK.

10. Promoted the obligation to implemented: both halves of its own narrow rule_text (UTF-8 enforcement, now proven; Layer Stack format conformance, already extensively covered by 33 pre-existing tests in the same file) are directly satisfied. Its capability sibling's much larger streaming-feature obligation remains correctly untouched and unaffected.
